findings.title: Off-by-one in `get`: index == len panics instead of returning None
`Sum_All` is not snake_case; the loop can be an iterator

passes.answer:
I've reviewed the PR context and the code. The repo is a single-file Rust crate (`src/lib.rs`), and the PR adds two public functions: `get` (bounds-checked item access) and `Sum_All` (i64 sum). Here's what I found:

**1. `get` panics exactly in the out-of-range case it exists to handle (critical).** The guard at `src/lib.rs:8` is `index <= items.len()`, so when `index == items.len()` the code takes the `Some(items[index])` branch and panics with "index out of bounds" instead of returning `None`. Trivial calls like `get(&[], 0)` or `get(&[1, 2, 3], 3)` crash, directly contradicting the doc comment "or `None` when it is out of range". The fix is `index < items.len()` — or, mirroring the existing `first` helper, the whole body can just be `items.get(index).copied()`. No tests were added anywhere in the PR; a one-line boundary test would have caught this immediately.

**2. `Sum_All` violates Rust naming conventions (minor).** Functions must be snake_case; `Sum_All` fires the warn-by-default `non_snake_case` lint on every build and is inconsistent with the crate's other functions (`first`, `get`). Since it's exported public API, renaming after merge would be a breaking change — it should be `sum_all` before this merges. The summation logic itself is correct (i64 accumulator, per-item cast before adding).
